issues.title: [Roadmap] Myelin model audit, cross-session collaboration, and UTXOPlay support (2026-11-02)
issues.body:
## Audit conclusion

**The model is sound in direction: continue building an evidence-bound, composable session runtime. Prioritize application protocols, portable evidence, and validation through real integrations.**

Current capabilities provide a foundation for deterministic records and replay in controlled-host games. Cross-service migration of scarce state, a unique canonical writer after ownership changes, and CKB adjudication of game results still need their own protocols and acceptance evidence. Having interfaces for each module does not establish end-to-end guarantees.

### Audit baseline and executed checks

- Local Myelin HEAD and GitHub main both pointed to `c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2` / 0.31.0.
- This audit ran `cargo test --locked --workspace`: **756 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored**. `cargo fmt --all --check` and `git diff --check` also passed.
- An isolated probe compiled against existing repository test fixtures without modifying source. With zero CellTx and `max_block_bytes=1,000,000`, a 1,000,001-byte handoff payload committed successfully. The field currently counts CellTx bytes only; aggregate frame/effect budgets need separate coverage.
- The same probe confirmed rejection of both unexpired handoffs without required evidence and expired handoffs. The existing test swaps the names of those IDs; the production gates are present.
- The full production gate, external Teeworlds workload, and public-testnet deployment were not rerun. The 0.31 release's historical devnet results are not evidence of a new deployment performed by this audit.
- Released UTXOPlay code was checked at `a81ef3ecd70dd551b24bdf62ad88c83610c1d473`, alongside newer local workspace changes and game repositories. **The local workspace contains substantial uncommitted/unreleased work; none was modified, committed, or deployed. Related issues distinguish observations from released behavior.**
- Before these issues were opened, Myelin #1–#5 were completed retrospective 0.31 records and there were no open issues. No existing UTXOPlay issues were found. Completed capabilities were not reopened.

## Model strengths and remaining limits

| Layer | Assessment | Next step |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ApplicationProfile and bounded frames | Binding program/schema/time/entropy/resources is the right direction | Make artifacts retrievable and replayable; bounded steps do not bound lifetime resources |
| CellDAG and strict VM | Separating scheduling from script validity is sound | Measure real workloads; zero VM cycles in host replay are not a performance conclusion |
| Finality, head CAS, checkpoint/outbox | Clear boundaries with atomic commit and recovery | Handle cloned stores across hosts, old authorities, and unknown journal outcomes |
| Command identity and admission | The 0.31 changes address useful boundaries with regression coverage | Supply durable source/reference adapters and adopt them downstream |
| Successor | Shared-store uniqueness, exact state, and reverse lineage are implemented | Define new-rule/codec migration, authorization, and command/reward inheritance |
| Handoff | Source commitment, target/expiry/evidence gates, and atomic shared-store consumption exist | Add source semantics, cancellation/refunds, cross-store proofs, and unique terminal states |
| CKB adapter and escrow | Preserve exact-transaction receipt levels and explicit application binding | Independently validate game-rule enforcement, DA, custody, and exits |

Native Rust host games and CellTx/CKB-VM use different execution integration modes. A signed Myelin game replay does not establish that CKB scripts executed or that CKB knows who won.

Persistent games may evolve through bounded sessions, epochs, and partitions. Finite Cells alone do not prove that every persistent world is impossible; session continuation alone does not prove unlimited-world capacity, recovery, or concurrency. The best initial validation targets are turn-based games, short matches, saves, seasonal results, and reward boundaries.

## Recommended cross-session architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph Games["Independent games with multiple sessions"]
    A["Game A: rooms, runs, and inventory"]
    B["Game B: rooms, runs, and inventory"]
    C["Game C: independent rules and authority"]
  end
  A --> LA["Independent canonical history and artifacts"]
  B --> LB["Independent canonical history and artifacts"]
  C --> LC["Independent canonical history and artifacts"]
  LA --> IDX["Rebuildable Registry and Evidence Index"]
  LB --> IDX
  LC --> IDX
  IDX --> R["Independent leaderboard verification, history, and achievements"]
  LA --> HP["Explicitly typed transfer or receipt protocol"]
  HP --> LB
  R --> AW["Optional issuance policy and idempotent jobs"]
  AW --> CK["CKB transactions and actual receipts"]
```

- **Successor:** a unique continuation of complete state for rule/authority evolution, not an arbitrary merge of two histories.
- **Handoff:** migration of an explicit object or right, requiring source locking/debiting, authorization, and target consumption. Delivering bytes does not establish safe migration of scarce rights.
- **Stitching/composition:** verification of multiple receipts and their causal relationships for achievements, tournaments, and audits. Copyable evidence does not necessarily need a global asset lock.
- **Collaboration:** independent sessions coordinate through asynchronous messages and explicit state machines. Initial scope excludes synchronous cross-game transactions, arbitrary remote calls, and store-wide shared state.
- **Shared versus separate stores:** a shared store can atomically arbitrate one terminal state. Independent services additionally need source proofs, canonical writers, and a cancellation/refund authority. Unknown outcomes remain pending; timeout alone is not a safe refund condition.

## Support UTXOPlay needs

Each independent game service may host multiple sessions, partitioned by actual player/run/room/inventory/season lifecycles. The platform continues to own identity, discovery, and query projections; games continue to own rules and state.

Prioritize reusable adapters, stable command recovery, historical artifacts, independently verified leaderboards, and composed results. Then pilot read-only cosmetics and testnet achievement issuance. Spore/DOB can express approved cosmetic/collectible identity, while earned coins and consumables remain under game rules. The [official Spore asset structure](https://docs.spore.pro/basics/technical-design/) does not verify game outcomes.

Use separate types and evidence for payments, eligibility, ownership, and settlement. A Fiber invoice or store ticket payment is not a proof of victory; wallet login does not authorize asset spending. Third-party browser-only or casual-replay games must not automatically receive a Myelin verification label.

## Delivery sequence

| Phase | Work | Release gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A: Near-term P1 | Protocol, clearer tests, aggregate budgets, source-effect authorization, journal, artifacts, and thin adapter | Preserve current claim boundaries and establish a runnable shared-store example |
| B: Product P1 | Shared-store transfer/cancellation, successors, fencing, archival; Registry, leaderboards, and two game integrations | Pass fault recovery, historical-save compatibility, unique consumption, and native/browser consistency |
| C: Controlled P2 | Remote proof/inbox, terminal-state coordination, and read-only cosmetics | Validate two independent stores; scarce migration requires unique terminal outcomes |
| D: On-chain P2 | Strict microgame court/exit and testnet issuance | Actual script/transaction evidence, explicit custody/issuer/DA assumptions, and reorg handling |

P1 identifies current foundation and product work; P2 depends on earlier acceptance gates. Protocol correctness for scarce rights blocks release of that capability, not continued operation of existing asset-free host-replay games.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S["Protocol, effects, limits, and tests"] --> L["Shared-store transfer and successor"]
  J["Journal, artifacts, and adapter"] --> U["Two game integrations, Registry, and leaderboard verification"]
  S --> J
  L --> F["Fencing and remote proofs"]
  F --> T["Unique remote terminal state"]
  J --> K["Strict game-to-CKB reference path"]
  U --> A["Read-only cosmetics and testnet achievements"]
  K --> A
  T --> X["Future cross-service scarce rights"]
```

## Detailed tasks

- [ ] [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7) — Define cross-session continuation, transfer, and evidence composition protocols
- [ ] [Myelin#8](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/8) — Separate handoff expiry, evidence-gate, and competing-consumer regression tests
- [ ] [Myelin#9](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/9) — Add aggregate budgets for handoffs, outbox effects, snapshots, and host execution
- [ ] [Myelin#10](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/10) — Validate source handoff and successor declarations through replayable application authorization
- [ ] [Myelin#11](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/11) — Implement a shared-store reference state machine for session transfer and cancellation
- [ ] [Myelin#12](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/12) — Provide a durable command journal and unknown-commit recovery reference adapter
- [ ] [Myelin#13](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/13) — Define portable session evidence bundles and reproducible replayer manifests
- [ ] [Myelin#14](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/14) — Add successor compatibility rules, migration evidence, and command inheritance semantics
- [ ] [Myelin#15](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/15) — Define cross-host writer fencing and session migration recovery
- [ ] [Myelin#16](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/16) — Support handoff proof bundles and an idempotent inbox across independent SessionStores
- [ ] [Myelin#17](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/17) — Define remote handoff terminal states, cancellation, and refund conditions
- [ ] [Myelin#18](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/18) — Complete archival, recovery budgets, and dependency retention for long-lived sessions
- [ ] [Myelin#19](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/19) — Build reusable game adapters and determinism, time, and randomness integration contracts
- [ ] [Myelin#20](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/20) — Measure latency, recovery, and session isolation with real game workloads
- [ ] [Myelin#21](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/21) — Split the production gate into portable, traceable CI acceptance lanes
- [ ] [Myelin#22](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/22) — Build a game-to-CKB testnet dispute and exit reference path with explicit evidence levels
- [ ] [UTXOPlay#2](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/2) — Build a rebuildable Session Registry and layered evidence index
- [ ] [UTXOPlay#3](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/3) — Verify leaderboards and cross-game achievements through independent replay and evidence composition
- [ ] [UTXOPlay#4](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/4) — Adopt Myelin 0.31 command recovery contracts per game while preserving historical saves
- [ ] [UTXOPlay#5](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/5) — Pilot read-only CKB cosmetic entitlements with explicit ownership and cross-game semantics
- [ ] [UTXOPlay#6](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/6) — Connect exact game results to testnet achievement issuance through idempotent reward jobs

## Definition of done

- [ ] Each task has positive, negative, and fault acceptance criteria; product-specific work remains in the appropriate game/platform repositories.
- [ ] Refresh documentation to distinguish shipped, reference, proposed, and deployed capabilities; remove stale topology and optimization-plan conclusions.
- [ ] Include version/rules/authority/trust bootstrap, resource limits, and retention policies in release contracts.
- [ ] At least two independent games adopt shared integration contracts while preserving historical replay verification.
- [ ] Performance/recovery reports cover real workloads and explicitly identify skipped or unsupported scope.
- [ ] Evidence from one stage is not used to substitute for another stage's requirements.

## Audit sources

[README](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/README.md), [session safety](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/docs/architecture/session-safety.md), [continuity](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/continuity.rs), [session core](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs), [RocksDB](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session-store-rocksdb/src/lib.rs), [replay](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/replay.rs), [production gate](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/scripts/myelin_production_gate.sh), [claim ladder](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/docs/security/claim-ladder.md), [released UTXOPlay boundaries](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/blob/a81ef3ecd70dd551b24bdf62ad88c83610c1d473/README.md), [released gateway](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/blob/a81ef3ecd70dd551b24bdf62ad88c83610c1d473/server/game-gateway.mjs).

This is an architecture, correctness-boundary, and product-integration audit with a work breakdown. It is not a complete security audit, deployment attestation, or performance certification.

issues.title: [P2] Support handoff proof bundles and an idempotent inbox across independent SessionStores
issues.body:
## Scenario

UTXOPlay games run as separate services with independent stores. Target B cannot load A's source block from B's SessionStore, so the existing shared-store handoff cannot directly cross services. A signed gRPC envelope and ACK-after-durability do not replace source-session finality or application authorization.

Start v1 with explicit targets and noneconomic results or controlled migration. Scarce rights remain gated on [Myelin#17](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/17).

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  S["Source commit and outbox in A"] --> R["Untrusted relay"]
  R --> I["Durable inbox in B"]
  I --> V["Verify source genesis, finality, and intake policy"]
  V --> T["Execute B candidate"]
  T --> C["Atomically commit target state, consumption, and receipt"]
  C --> A["Return consumption proof asynchronously"]
```

## Deliverables

- Version Export/Verify/Import ports binding source genesis/configuration, exact block hash/height/root, handoff-commitment inclusion, complete source proof, target, payload schema, authorization, and evidence requirements.
- Resolve source authority and consensus configuration through trusted allowlists/policies. Do not trust arbitrary self-signed keys supplied in a bundle.
- Preserve the existing local interface's shared-store semantics. Cross-store intake needs explicit verified results and durable import records, not fabricated load_block success.
- Deduplicate inbox entries by canonical source namespace and handoff ID. Detect tampering, reordering, and equivocation; bound size, dependencies, and depth before verification.
- Bind intake verification to the application profile. Import is not consumption; recheck and record consumption at target commit.
- Allow duplicate/late delivery, lost ACKs, and restart recovery. Transport is at least once; authoritative commits supply business deduplication.
- Actually verify the required evidence stage. Network signatures, nonempty bytes, and receipt counts are not independent evidence.
- One-time consumption for an exact target depends on its unique canonical writer/history. Safety across cloned targets depends on [Myelin#15](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/15).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two processes with independent RocksDB stores and different authorities can export/import/consume without sharing a database.
- [ ] Correctly handle forged source proofs, wrong genesis/profile/target, changed payloads, missing evidence, and duplicate delivery.
- [ ] Recover from lost ACKs before/after consumption, source-service outages, and relay restarts.
- [ ] Offline bundles include source dependencies needed to replay the target independently.
- [ ] Reject unsupported remote policy targets instead of implying global uniqueness.

Depends on [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7), [Myelin#10](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/10), [Myelin#13](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/13), [Myelin#9](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/9); related: [Myelin#17](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/17), [Myelin#11](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/11). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[Current shared-store reads](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/lib.rs#L1101), [network envelope](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session-network/proto/session_network.proto), [continuity types](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session/src/continuity.rs).

issues.title: [P2][RFC] Define remote handoff terminal states, cancellation, and refund conditions
issues.body:
## Counterexample to solve first

A locks one item for B. B finalizes its credit, but the consumption receipt is lost in transit. If A refunds on timeout, the player has rights in both A and B. Correct signatures and transport deduplication do not prevent this error.

Shared-store consumption can compete over one RocksDB key. Copying that key into separate services does not preserve its uniqueness guarantee.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> SourceLocked
  SourceLocked --> TargetPending: Deliver proof
  TargetPending --> TargetFinal: Unique target finalizes consumption
  TargetFinal --> SourceCompleted: Return consumption proof
  SourceLocked --> CancelFinal: Authoritative cancellation
  TargetPending --> CancelFinal: Prove target can no longer finalize consumption
  CancelFinal --> Refunded
  TargetPending --> InDoubt: Partition or unknown outcome
  InDoubt --> TargetFinal: Find final consumption proof
  InDoubt --> CancelFinal: Obtain mutually exclusive cancellation proof
```

## Questions the RFC must answer

- Who ultimately decides uniqueness: a shared authoritative claim service, canonical target consensus, or an L1 claim/escrow Cell? State trust, availability, and cost for each option.
- Prefer one fixed target initially. Disable forwarding, remote multi-target policy competition, and automatic refunds. Unknown outcomes remain locked; establish recoverable safety before adding liveness mechanisms.
- Cancellation requires a verifiable terminal outcome that permanently excludes future consumption. Local absence or wall-clock expiry cannot prove a remote target has not consumed.
- Align target deadlines with source refund conditions. Consider old timestamps, delayed finality, clock differences, and offline recipients.
- Any on-chain design must specify how scripts constrain both consumption and refund. "Use CKB as a nullifier" is insufficient.
- Define behavior for different authorities/quorums, malicious relays, conflicting source declarations, cloned target stores, reorgs, and retention periods.
- State conservation invariants, canonical-history assumptions, and responsibilities. Do not advertise synchronous atomic cross-session calls without cross-store atomicity.
- Exchanges involving two transfers need their own failure/compensation protocol; an ordinary saga does not establish trustless atomic exchange.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A transition table specifies evidence, actor, durable location, and irreversible point for every step.
- [ ] Rights cannot duplicate when B finalizes but loses its ACK, when cancellation races consumption, or when two target copies run.
- [ ] Model/fault-injection tests cover partitions, restarts, reordering, and long delays. Progress may stop to preserve safety.
- [ ] The reference implementation uses test assets and exposes its L1/authority assumptions and unsupported capabilities.
- [ ] Keep scarce-asset features disabled until these criteria pass.

Depends on [Myelin#7](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/7), [Myelin#11](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/11), [Myelin#16](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/16), [Myelin#15](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/15); used by [UTXOPlay#6](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/6). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

issues.title: [P2] Build a game-to-CKB testnet dispute and exit reference path with explicit evidence levels
issues.body:
## Capability to validate

Authority-signed game replays do not automatically establish CKB adjudication. Myelin already supplies projection, adapter receipts, devnet smoke tests, and escrow integration. Those foundations do not establish a complete public-testnet game court/DA path.

Choose a small game-state transition replayable in strict CKB-VM, complete the reference flow, and then decide which results of larger games warrant on-chain enforcement.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  O["Test-asset opening and explicit custody rules"] --> X["Off-chain execution under a strict profile"]
  X --> D["Retrievable inputs, state, and evidence"]
  D --> C["Exact disputed chunk and court input"]
  C --> V["Actual CKB script verification"]
  V --> S["Normal settlement or timeout exit"]
  S --> R["Exact transaction receipts and reorg handling"]
```

## Scope

- Start with a tiny turn-based/fixed-rule fixture binding the same program, schema, VM profile, inputs, pre/post roots, and authorization.
- Specify actual transactions and verifier artifacts enforcing opening, updates, challenges, normal close, timeout/abort, and unique consumption.
- Distinguish off-chain application correctness, committee attestation, DA, CKB script validity, and inclusion/confirmation. Generic carrier success cannot substitute for on-chain game-rule adjudication.
- Define assets, participants, expiry, capacity, fees, and exits. Existing fixed-participant escrow does not automatically supply an open game economy.
- Use a shared authoritative custody/single-spend domain for normal and recovery exits, preventing withdrawals from both old and new states.
- Independently verify retrievable data through a DA/recovery provider; the operator's local disk is not independent DA.
- Complete a devnet fixture without real funds first. Public-testnet deployment needs its own configuration and execution record. This issue tracks design/implementation, not a deployment performed by the audit.
- Include negative execution evidence for invalid game results, wrong proofs, duplicate claims, stale-state exits, timeout disputes, and reorgs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Demonstrate an incorrect game transition rejected by a CKB script, not only by host validation.
- [ ] Reproduce open/commit/challenge/settle and timeout exit with actual transactions, script hashes, and network genesis.
- [ ] Locally reverify receipts and report accepted, committed, and configured-depth confirmed separately.
- [ ] Do not assert production/mainnet safety or permissionless L2 security before their separate evidence requirements are met.
- [ ] Publish instructional documentation and test-asset drill evidence so [UTXOPlay#6](https://github.com/UTXOPlay/UTXOPlay/issues/6) can select the appropriate result-assurance level.

Depends on [Myelin#10](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/10), [Myelin#13](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/13), [Myelin#21](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/21); economic cross-session transfer also depends on [Myelin#17](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/17). Roadmap: [Myelin#6](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/issues/6).

[Claim ladder](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/docs/security/claim-ladder.md), [testnet runbook](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/docs/public-testnet-rehearsal-runbook.md), [escrow](https://github.com/Myelin-Labs/Myelin/blob/c0ac291c03ed8996e62834cb3f480e1ce8dc09a2/session-escrow/src/lib.rs).
